Original descriptor as written by juror

Intermediate standardization step

text:
A reference dictionary for mapping taste descriptors to standardized terms. Includes original, translated, and simplified versions. Designed for generic/widely-used sensory attributes.



dictionary_generic




A data frame with 64 rows and 3 columns:


original


Original or raw descriptor (often in French)


translated


English translation


translated_simple


Simplified/harmonized English form





Used by data harmonization functions (e.g., harmonize_terms()) to standardize taste terminology across panelists and sessions.



doi:10.1016/j.crfs.2025.101043; Zenodo https://zenodo.org/records/14616396




library("sapid")

data(dictionary_generic)
head(dictionary_generic)

  original translated translated_simple
1    BOISÉ      WOODY             WOODY
2   AQUEUX                             
3   VOLUME     VOLUME            VOLUME
4    UMAMI      UMAMI             UMAMI
5    FRAIS      FRESH             FRESH
6     SALÉ      SALTY             SALTY

# Example lookup
subset(dictionary_generic, original == "BOISÉ")

  original translated translated_simple
1    BOISÉ      WOODY             WOODY

The primary sensory panel dataset containing taste profile ratings for Swertia chirayita sample fractions. Includes original (as entered by panelists) and harmonized (standardized) taste descriptor terms. This is the main table for sensory-MS correlation analyses.



profiles




A data frame with 1,665 rows and 6 columns:


fraction


Fraction identifier (e.g., "fraction_17")


session


Session identifier (e.g., "session_01")


jury


Juror identifier (e.g., "jury_03")


taste_original


Original taste descriptor as entered by panelist


taste_harmonized


Standardized/harmonized taste descriptor


value


Numerical rating or intensity score





Missing or empty harmonized values indicate descriptors that could not be consistently mapped across panelists or were deemed non-informative (e.g., "RIEN" meaning "nothing"). Use !is.na(taste_harmonized) & taste_harmonized != ““ to filter for valid descriptors in analyses.

text:
Filter profiles to keep only taste descriptors that are consistently used across multiple panelists (minimum jury threshold).



load_consistent_profiles(input, min_jury = 2L)







input


Input data frame or file path to profiles table




min_jury


Minimum number of jurors who must use a taste descriptor for it to be kept. Default: 2.






This function filters sensory data to keep only taste descriptors that appear consistently across at least min_jury panelists. It removes descriptors that are used by only one panelist (potentially idiosyncratic terms).



Data frame with consistent profiles and grouped statistics




library("sapid")

data(profiles)
consistent <- load_consistent_profiles(profiles, min_jury = 2)
nrow(consistent)

title: sapid
text:
Replace terms in a given string using a dictionary, with intelligent matching and case-insensitive handling.



harmonize_terms(dictionary, x, mode = "word", fallback = FALSE)







dictionary


Path to the dictionary file, a data frame containing replacement terms, or NULL to use cached environment dictionaries




x


Character string to be cleaned




mode


Replacement mode: ‘word’ for word boundary matching, ‘substring’ for partial matching, ‘fixed’ for fast fixed-string matching




fallback


Logical, whether to fall back to original string if no replacements occur






For better performance when calling this function repeatedly on many strings, pass a pre-loaded dictionary data frame instead of a file path. The function uses base R replacement helpers for all modes to avoid an extra dependency.



Character string with terms replaced




library("sapid")

# Using data frame dictionary (faster)
data(dictionary_generic)
harmonize_terms(
  dictionary = dictionary_generic,
  x = "Some text with specific terms"
)

# Using file path (legacy, slower)
harmonize_terms(
  dictionary = "path/to/dictionary.csv",
  x = "Some text with specific terms"
)

title: sapid
text:
A reference dictionary specifically for napping session terminology, mapping napping-specific descriptors to standardized terms.



dictionary_napping




A data frame with 45 rows and 2 columns:


original


Original napping descriptor


translated


Standardized descriptor





Napping methods often generate unique terminology or abbreviations (e.g., "_LEGER" for "light"). This dictionary maps these to harmonized forms used in broader analyses.



doi:10.1016/j.crfs.2025.101043; Zenodo https://zenodo.org/records/14616396




library("sapid")

data(dictionary_napping)
head(dictionary_napping)

2      _LEGER       _LOW
3     _LEGERE       _LOW
4     _FAIBLE       _LOW
5 -MOYEN-FORT           
6   _MLOYENNE           

# Find mappings for "LEGER"
subset(dictionary_napping, grepl("LEGER", original))
